questions.q: An hourly series has a daily pattern. Which STL period do you use?
why: 7 is for daily data with a weekly pattern.
168 is the weekly period for hourly data.

questions.q: What do you score after STL?
why: The trend is the slow movement.
Correct: residual = what the model did not explain.
The seasonal part is the expected pattern.

questions.q: Scenario: a Saturday has 300 orders. Typical Saturday is 500, typical Tuesday is 200. The overall z-score of 300 is small. What do you conclude?
options: It may be a seasonal anomaly; check the residual
why: It is normal only compared with all days, not with other Saturdays.
Correct: compare with the expected Saturday value.
Nothing shows the data is wrong.

questions.q: Generalized ESD: you set r = 10. The test says 3 outliers. What does this mean?
options: At most 10 were allowed, and 3 pass the test
why: r is only an upper limit.
Correct: the largest i with R(i) > λ(i) is 3.
A result of 3 is a valid output.

questions.q: Scenario: you fit STL on the whole last year of data and then alert on the last week. What is wrong?
options: The fit used the last week, so the model partly learned the anomaly (leakage)
why: In a live system, the last week is not known when you fit.
Correct: fit on the past, then score new points.
STL works on a year of data.
